# Reading your documents — what ctxEco takes, and what it keeps

You are about to let ctxEco **read** documents in your cloud storage. This goes
further than mapping. Mapping reads names and structure; this reads what is
inside the files.

Please read this before you agree. We store the exact words on this page
alongside your decision, so that later there is no argument about what you were
told.

## What happens when you agree

1. **We download the full contents** of the supported documents in the folders
   you choose, including everything nested inside them.
2. **We store a copy** of each of those documents in your workspace's private
   storage inside ctxEco, separate from every other customer's.
3. **We index the text**, so that it can be searched, retrieved, and **quoted
   back word for word in answers** — to you, and to other people in your
   workspace.

We also read everything listed in the mapping disclosure — names, paths, sizes,
dates, owners and sharing structure — because a document is more useful when we
know where it sat and who worked on it.

## Which documents

Documents whose file type ctxEco supports. Anything else is skipped, and the
result tells you how many files were skipped. Where a file type is supported, the
whole of its content is read; we do not read part of a document.

## Indexing means the text is processed

To make a document searchable, its text has to pass through the inference
service configured for your workspace. That processing is what indexing is. Your
workspace's configuration determines which service that is and where it runs.

Neither ctxEco nor the model providers ctxEco uses train models on your content.

## Who can see it afterwards

The connection is made with your account, so ctxEco can only read what you can
already see in your storage. That is a limit on what gets read. **It is not, by
itself, a limit on who can see it afterwards.**

Once a document is in your workspace, other people in that workspace may be able
to retrieve it and to receive passages of it quoted in an answer, even if they
could not open the original file in your storage. You can narrow that with your
workspace's own access controls, but it is not narrow by default. This matters
more here than it does for a map, because what can come back here is the text
itself.

Please choose folders on that basis, and not on the basis of what you personally
are able to open.

## Other people's documents may be in your folders

Personal and shared drives usually hold material other people sent you, or that
other people own, or that belongs to a client. Reading it into ctxEco is a
decision you are making about their documents too, and often it is not yours
alone to make. Choose the narrowest set of folders that is actually useful, and
leave out anything you were given in confidence.

## What this permission covers

Only the folders named in this consent record, and everything nested inside
them. Anything recorded here as an exclusion is not read. This permission does
not extend to any other site, drive or folder — each of those needs its own
consent and its own record. It is also not a mapping consent: reading names and
structure has its own disclosure and its own record.

## We never change anything in your storage

Reading is one-way. ctxEco does not create, rename, move, overwrite or delete
anything in your storage. **It never deletes one of your files — not in this
feature, not anywhere else in this product, under any setting, ever.**

## Withdrawing this permission — and what withdrawing does not do

You can withdraw this permission at any time, from your connector settings.

Withdrawing is recorded as a **new, separate event**. The record of your
original decision is never altered and never deleted, so the history of what was
permitted, by whom, and when stays intact and can be examined later. We do not
read under a permission that has been withdrawn: no new documents, and no
re-reading of documents that change afterwards.

**Withdrawing does not, by itself, remove what has already been read.** The
copies already in your workspace stay there, and stay searchable and quotable,
until they are deleted. Deleting them is a separate action, it is available to
you at any time from your own file list, and it removes both the stored copy and
its index from ctxEco. Deleting them does not touch anything in your storage —
your original documents are unaffected by anything you do here.

If you want both, do both: withdraw to stop future reading, and delete to remove
what was already read.

## What we do not do with it

We do not sell your documents. We do not share them with other ctxEco
customers — your workspace is isolated from every other workspace. We do not use
them to train models.
